question: In 1991 Billboard's album chart switched from shop reports to counting barcode scans at tills. What happened?
answer: Country and rap rose. The old chart relied on staff at selected shops reporting what sold best, which record labels could lobby and big-city stores dominated. Once SoundScan counted real sales, Garth Brooks and N.W.A reached No. 1 within months. The audience had been there all along, uncounted.
move: Before trusting a ranking, ask who was doing the reporting.
trap: Assuming a chart built from shop reports already measured real sales.
reference: Billboard, first Billboard 200 chart compiled from Nielsen SoundScan data, issue of 25 May 1991
